paras: The Sulphur Springs whippings were the public whipping of a Black school-teacher and about twenty Black men by a party of whites at Sulphur Springs, Bowie county, on September 16, 1903. The teacher was whipped for reportedly making insulting remarks about a young white woman, and the others for protesting his whipping; they were then warned to go to work or leave town. The episode is known from a single New Orleans wire dispatch printed in the New York Sun.

According to the dispatch, a Black school-teacher who was said to have made insulting remarks about a young white woman was whipped publicly by whites in Sulphur Springs. Some of the Black residents who watched "grew indignant and denounced the outrage." The crowd then seized them as well and gave each "a sound thrashing," warning that unless they went to work "very quickly" they would have to move out of town.

The dispatch stressed that there was "no attempt at concealment": the men were whipped in the streets in front of a large crowd. Its headline put the number whipped at "a score," but none of the victims or whippers was named.
No report of arrests, an investigation, or any departure of the men from the town appears in the coverage.

The New York Sun printed the dispatch on September 17 under the headline "WHIPPED THE IDLE NEGROES," with a subhead saying a score of them were "Punished by Whites for Resenting a Beating a Teacher Received." The item took over the whippers' terms, calling the victims "idle negroes" and stating the teacher's alleged insult as fact, and it added no comment of its own. The word "outrage" appears only as the Black onlookers' description of the teacher's whipping.
The dispatch gave Bowie county but no state, and no local report, follow-up, or Black-press account of the whippings was found.

A negro school-teacher, having made insulting remarks about a young white woman, was publicly whipped.
Some of the negroes who witnessed the whipping grew indignant and denounced the outrage.
warning them that unless they should go to work very quickly they would have to move out of town.
